sections.h2: What does the Rowan County Register of Deeds office do?
sections.html:
The county describes the register's duty as the integrity, completeness, accuracy and safekeeping of every public record recorded in the office. For a house seller, that means the deed that moves title to the buyer and the deed of trust that secures a loan both live there.

The office offers more than land records. It lists online certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, where identity is verified through an online system and a vendor adds a small convenience fee, and it serves as a passport acceptance facility. Those services help families settling an estate, who often need death certificates to support a deed or probate filing.

sections.h2: How does e-recording work in Rowan County?
sections.html:
Rowan County started electronic recording in August 2010 and accepts electronically submitted documents, maps included. The county says this helps banks, title companies, law firms and other businesses in real estate deals.

The county lists these benefits of e-recording:

  • No travel time or travel cost to reach the counter
  • No check writing, since fees are handled electronically
  • Document security
  • Real-time tracking of document status
  • A quick return of the recording information and a stamped image
  • An easy start for new users

An individual seller does not usually sign up for this. The closing attorney or title company that handles the Rowan County sale will already use a vendor from the county's vendor list.

sections.h2: How does Property Check protect a Rowan County owner?
sections.html:
It emails or texts you when a filing appears under a name or parcel number you register. The county is direct about why: the register does not decide whether a document is genuine, so a fraudulent paper that meets statutory recording requirements and has the fees paid can still enter the record.

Property Check is free, runs around the clock and sends alerts through the contact method you pick. The county admits it cannot block a bad filing, only warn you quickly. If you suspect fraud, call local law enforcement. Owners of vacant or inherited houses in Rowan County gain the most, because nobody is otherwise looking at the record. Questions on the system go to 704-216-8636.

sections.h2: How do I record a map or survey in Rowan County?
sections.html:
Have the Rowan County Review Officer sign the map first, then bring it to the register on one of three sizes: 18 by 24 inches, 21 by 30 inches or 24 by 36 inches. Review Officers work in the Planning Office and the Tax Assessor's office on the second floor at 402 N Main Street in Salisbury.

You get the original back after recording, and the office keeps a digital copy. The county says to ask about electronic map recording. If your lot sits in a recorded subdivision or you hold a recorded survey, a copy costs $2 at the register's counter. Sellers sometimes order one to settle a boundary question before a buyer's survey.

sections.h2: What does North Carolina charge on a Rowan County deed?
sections.html:
Recording fees are uniform across the state and the grantor pays the excise tax, so the Rowan County register collects the same amounts as other counties. The statutes print these figures:

Statutory charges at the Rowan County register
ItemStatute amount
General instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages
Added pages$4.00 each
Cancellation or satisfactionNo fee
Excise tax$1.00 for each $500 or fractional part

The register collects the tax before the deed is recorded. Half goes to the county general fund and half to the state, and a parcel that spans two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value. The statute calls the recording fees complete and exclusive.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter when I sell?
sections.html:
A conveyance, option or long lease has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Registration time sets priority between competing instruments.

Closing attorneys therefore hold funds until the deed is ready to go on the record. Ask yours to confirm that earlier mortgages were released and that any transfer from an heir or ex-spouse already appears in the Rowan County record.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Rowan County house?
sections.html:
A death transfer starts at the clerk of superior court, not at the register. For a small intestate estate, an heir may file an affidavit with the clerk in the county where the person lived once 30 days have passed since the death. The statute's limit is $20,000 of personal property, or up to $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the sole heir, and the affidavit lists each tract of real property owned.

Larger estates need a personal representative. After that, the paper that shows who can sign the deed is what the register records, so ask a probate attorney before listing. A buyer's title insurer will want the right authority on record, and Property Check can watch the parcel while the house sits empty.

faqs.q: When did Rowan County start electronic recording?
faqs.a: The Rowan County Register of Deeds began electronic recording in August 2010, and the office accepts electronically submitted documents including maps.
Yes. You create an account, list a name or parcel number and choose how to be alerted when a filing is recorded.

faqs.q: Which map sizes can be recorded in Rowan County?
faqs.a: The county accepts 18 by 24, 21 by 30 and 24 by 36 inches. The Rowan County Review Officer must sign before the map goes to the register.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Rowan County deed?
faqs.a: The seller, as transferor, pays it to the register before recording at $1.00 for each $500 or fractional part of the price.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded survey cost?
faqs.a: The county says a copy of a recorded subdivision map or survey costs $2 at the Register of Deeds.
